result.title: AdaAlloc: Adaptive Visual Token Allocation for Long-Video Question Answering
result.summary: Long-video question answering forces multimodal large language models to reason under strict visual-token budgets, creating a tradeoff between broad temporal coverage and fine-grained spatial detail. Uniform sampling preserves coverage but often obscures decisive local cues, while caption-based or frame-similarity retrieval operates over lossy proxies that can miss motion, state changes, and before-after relations. We recast long-video reasoning as a visual-token allocation problem: given a fixed budget, decide how much to spend on global context versus high-resolution local evidence, and where in the video to draw that local evidence from. We introduce AdaAlloc, a training-free inference framework that adaptively allocates visual tokens between a global video overview and localized visual detail. AdaAlloc first plans a global/local allocation policy, then uses temporal grounding to locate candidate evidence segments and refines them into a compact temporal memory. The selected policy controls both frame sampling density and resolution, combining sparse, lower-resolution global frames with denser, higher-resolution local frames drawn from the refined memory. The final answerer reasons over the allocated global context and refined local evidence. Across LVBench, MLVU, VideoMME, and LongVideoBench, AdaAlloc improves over budget-matched uniform sampling by up to 10.5 percentage points and outperforms the compared frame-selection and agentic methods on their reported benchmarks.

AI.brief_summary: 研究长视频问答在固定视觉 token 预算下如何权衡全局覆盖与局部细节，提出免训练推理框架 AdaAlloc：先规划全局/局部预算比例，再用时序定位找出候选片段并精炼为紧凑时序记忆，按策略组合稀疏低分辨率全局帧与密集高分辨率局部帧供最终作答。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应「视觉证据筛选」与预算分配问题，可作为固定 token 预算下全局/局部取舍的对照基线；其分配只作用于输入 token 而非内部 latent 状态，因此可供核查 latent 方法能否以更低成本取得同类证据针对性收益。
